segments.text: What if the Sun cranked up 10%?
The solar constant measures the mean electromagnetic radiation per square metre at one astronomical unit.
Satellites record about 1.361 kW / m² at solar minimum and roughly 0.1 % higher at solar maximum.
A ten‑percent increase would simply be a ten‑percent higher value of that constant.
The definition of the solar constant does not include any claim about how such a change would feel on Earth, only that it is a flux density measured at a fixed distance.
